role.title: Research Assistant
role.company: University of Colorado Boulder, College of Engineering & Applied Science
role.summary: Worked on Adapton, an incremental computing system, and built a Rust visualization tool for research on typed incremental computation.
role.content:
Worked with Dr. Matthew Hammer on a programming language for Adapton, an incremental computing system.

Developed an online visualization tool for the paper "Fungi: Typed incremental computation with names," using Rust and programming language theory.

projects.title: Fungi Incremental Computation Visualizer
projects.summary: An online visualization tool for the paper 'Fungi: Typed incremental computation with names.'
projects.content: Built an interactive visualization tool in Rust to accompany research on typed incremental computation with names. The project made the programming language output explorable in a browser.

profile.name: Ryan Vandersmith
profile.tagline: R&D software engineer building forecasting, visualization, and analysis tools for meteorology and atmospheric science.
profile.summary: Ryan Vandersmith is an R&D software engineer with 10+ years of experience and a deep self-taught background in meteorology. He builds weather forecasting and analysis tools used by photographers, storm chasers, and researchers, including Mesoview (skychaser.mesoview.app), a cloud inversion forecast tool, a mountain wave visualization tool, and a stepwise CAPE/CIN contribution to SounderPy. Professionally, he worked on Caffeine.ai, an AI website builder, and led Motoko programming-language tooling, including a VS Code extension with more than 85,000 installs. He also has experience with cross-chain EVM integrations, developer-experience products, UX research, Rust research software at the University of Colorado Boulder, consulting, and public-sector software.
expertise: weather forecasting and atmospheric analysis tools
